To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a photoselecting greenhouse cover did not affect the ability of the aphid parasitoid Aphidius ervii to locate and parasitize the aphid Macrosiphum euphoria in a lettuce crop.
the performance and host-finding ability of the aphid parasitoid Aphis ervi were not affected by the use of a photoseselective cover.
photoselective net did not affect the parasitoid ability to parasitize the aphid host.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a more sustainable pest management system in protected crops.

improving the knowledge about how photoselective screens could be used in combination with biological control to reduce pest populations and to improve the sustainability of greenhouse vegetable production.

the use of UV-absorbing net in vegetable crops as a strategy to reduce pest damage, and the use of biological control agents to reduce the use of chemical insecticides in the control of aphids in greenhouse crops.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photoselectivity of the cover has no effect on the performance of A. erviv.
photoselective nets do not have a negative effect on the performance and the host finding ability of A. ervi.
the use of UV-absorbing greenhouse covers does not have any negative effect on the performance of A. ervis and therefore it can be implemented in vegetable crops where it is used to control aphids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
photoselective nets are not detrimental for the performance of this parasitoid.
photoselective nets could be a good tool to improve the performance of parasitoids, and that the use of these nets would not be a limiting factor for the parasitism of the host by A. ervi.
the use of photoselective nets is a suitable strategy to improve crop production in greenhouses and, in addition, does not seem to have a negative impact on biological control agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photoselecting greenhouse cover used did not interfere with the host finding ability of the parasitoid.
UV-absorbing netting does not seem to affect the performance of A. erviv, which is a promising biological control agent for the control of M. euphorbiae.
